style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: A desktop private-share clearing register in a clean isometric cutaway on a warm oak desk. A single coated paper stock certificate folio sits in a shallow aluminium docking tray on a short rail. Above it a raised brushed-steel round-price shelf; beside it a lower slate-grey secondary clearing tray set at a visible drop below, joined by a short modular connector. One directional key light rakes from the left, throwing long contact shadows. Matte surfaces, visible seams, no text, no lettering. Palette: bone white, graphite, ochre. Asymmetric isometric cutaway with the register off-centre left and empty desk to right.
rationale: The article explains a structural pricing mechanism with two prices for one share, which suits an axonometric cutaway showing the routing and drop between primary round price and secondary clearing price. It avoids a photographic still of a single object and keeps the systemic tension legible.
cue: nine percent below its company's last round price
subject: a single share certificate folio routed through two pricing trays in a private share clearing register, one raised round-price tray and one lower secondary clearing tray
core_thesis: Your grant is quoted at a round price, but the median private share cleared nine percent below that round price on the secondary market while record valuations were set by a fifth fewer deals.
core_conflict: Primary round price versus secondary market clearing price, with thinning deal volume amplifying the fragility of the quoted mark.
composition: asymmetric isometric cutaway with the register off-centre left and empty desk to right
alt_text: Isometric bone-white register with a brushed-steel dial, a tray of cream cards and an empty slate-grey tray on pale oak, lit from the left.
caption: Two prices for one share: one tray holds the round's price, the other is where a holder clears at a discount.
title: Nobody Pays Your Round'S Price

review.depicts: A beige and grey isometric mechanical unit sits on a light wood desk, with a circular brushed-metal dial on top, a sliding carriage holding a stack of blank pale sheets banded in gold on a raised left tray, and a separate empty dark-grey shallow tray at lower right, with bare wood to the right.
review.reason: The raised loaded tray versus the lower empty tray routing a document folio does map to the round-price mark against the discounted secondary clearing price, but with no certificate, ticker or price cues the device reads at first glance as generic office hardware rather than private-share clearing.
